info.bio:
Duran Duran nació en 1978 en Birmingham (Inglaterra). Sus fundadores fueron Nick Rhodes, John Taylor, Simon Colley y Stephen Duffy. El nombre de Duran Duran fue tomado del personaje que interpretaba Milo O'Shea en la película de ciencia-ficción Barbarella, protagonizada por Jane Fonda.

En 1979, Colley y Duffy son sustituídos por el cantante Andy Wicket y el batería Roger Taylor. Además, gracias a un anuncio aparecido en prensa, eligen a Andy Taylor como nuevo guitarrista de la banda.

scenes.name: Segunda invasión británica y MTV
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1982 el new pop deja de ser un sueño de periodistas: «Don't You Want Me», «Tainted Love» y «The Look of Love» anuncian una nueva invasión, y en 1983 la segunda camada (Duran Duran, Culture Club, Wham!, Eurythmics, Thompson Twins) conquista Estados Unidos gracias a MTV, canal ideado por Michael Nesmith que, sin vídeos americanos, dependía de los británicos, más videogénicos y cultivados en el estilo («I want my MTV»). A Flock of Seagulls, Altered Images («Happy Birthday»), Simple Minds («Promised You a Miracle», New Gold Dream), Haircut 100, Kajagoogoo; Bowie se broncea con «Let's Dance». El new pop reexporta música negra (Chic, P-Funk, Quincy Jones) a la América blanca. En el Reino Unido, 1983 se vive en cambio como un año infausto: reelección de Thatcher, «Kill Ugly Pop» en las paredes y la vuelta de la conciencia social.

scenes.name: Synth-pop y new romantics
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Todo empieza con los instrumentos electrónicos, el futurismo melódico de Eno y los ritmos robóticos de Kraftwerk: el synth-pop es quizá el acontecimiento más importante de la música melódica desde el Mersey-beat. The Buggles («Video Killed The Radio Star»), Gary Numan, Yellow Magic Orchestra, OMD, Depeche Mode, Human League; con Soft Cell llega el diluvio y el dúo de teclista y cantante se impone (Eurythmics, Yazoo, Erasure, Pet Shop Boys). Flying Lizards y New Order («Blue Monday»). Los nuevos ídolos adolescentes, los new romantics: Duran Duran, Culture Club, Thompson Twins, Tears For Fears, ABC, Heaven 17.

scenes.name: Nuevos románticos
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Movimiento londinense que rescata del glam el maquillaje y la pose, con un uso coyuntural de la tecnología: Ultravox (con John Foxx primero), Japan, Visage de Steve Strange, Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, ABC, la pose kraftwerkiana de Gary Numan y, después, Culture Club.

podcast.title: Age of Consent Protocol on American Tours (Post-1981)
podcast.body: During American tours after 1981, Duran Duran implemented a system to prevent legal issues related to sexual consent. Their daily itineraries included a code number at the bottom, which indicated the age of consent (18, 20, or 21) for the specific state they were in. This proactive measure aimed to avoid "awkward legal problems." "Those numbers signified the age of consent for whatever state they happen to be in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Best-Known New Wave Band (1982)
podcast.body: Active by 1982, Duran Duran was arguably "the best known of all the so-called New Wave bands." Their telegenic presence was perfectly suited for the rise of music videos on channels like MTV, which significantly propelled their global fame and solidified their status as New Wave icons. "Durand Durand from 1982, they were probably the best known of all the so-called New Wave bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initiating "A View to a Kill" Theme (1985)
podcast.body: The idea for Duran Duran to create the "A View to a Kill" theme originated with their bass player, Roger Taylor. While reportedly drunk at a party, Taylor approached producer Cubby Broccoli and challenged him about getting "someone decent to do one of your theme songs," an unexpected approach that surprisingly led to the band getting the commission. "Actually it was bass player Roger Taylor who had the idea. He was drunk at a party and he wandered up to producer Cubby Broccoli and said something very close to this. When are you going to get someone decent to do one of your theme songs?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Hungry Like a Wolf" Music Video
podcast.body: The music video for "Hungry Like a Wolf" is cited as a memorable and "crazy" example of storytelling in the medium, representing the kind of iconic work whose creative process music video directors would enjoy discussing. "So imagine if you could go back in the days and sit down with Durand Ran and talk about the hungry like a wolf video like what the hell could tell you guys being this jungle and just going through this crazy, crazy story and sitting down with like the best of the best and hearing their stories of the director is working with Madonna and working with the stones and that's the beauty about the show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Connoisseur Wine and Champagne Selection
podcast.body: Duran Duran's rider featured a highly specific section for "Wine and Champagne," detailing an impressive cellar-worthy selection. It required three bottles of excellent quality Italian red wine (Sassicaia, Solaia, or Tignanello) from vintages between 1989 and 1997. Additionally, two bottles of excellent white wine (Corton-Charlemagne preferred) from vintages 1996, 1999, 2001, 2002, or 2004, and two bottles of good quality champagne (Moët & Chandon or Bollinger preferred) were requested. "Three bottles of excellent quality Italian red wine. Saskassia, Soleia or Trigonello. Vintage is between 1989 and 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Specific Tequila Brand
podcast.body: The rider also included a demand for one bottle of Patrón Silver tequila, with a direct warning: "do not supply regular tequila," indicating a preference for a specific premium brand. "Do not supply regular tequila."

podcast.title: Featured on 80s US New Wave Compilations
podcast.body: In the 1980s, compilations edited as "New Wave" in the United States often featured a diverse range of British bands, including Duran Duran, reflecting how the term was applied to non-mainstream UK music. These compilations were often a "mixed bag" of artists. "Tienen a los Smith, tienen a Durán, tienen a New Order, tienen todo un poco mezclado, todo que venía prácticamente al reino nido que no era música de grandísimo, con sumo se le se le acaba llamando New Wave."

"Now you could tell by listening that these artists grew up listening to groups like Durand Oran, Joy Division, The Cure, New Order, Pixies, The Police and You too."

podcast.title: MTV Breakthrough
podcast.body: By the end of 1982, Duran Duran was aggressively using the music video medium, releasing their *Rio* album with glossy videos shot in exotic locales by director Russell Mulcahy, finally breaking into the American market. A US radio remix also helped. "But by the end of 1982, no band was selling themselves harder in the music video medium than Durand Durand."

podcast.body: Part of the wave of "fun, fresh music" from the UK that became popular in North America due to exposure on MTV in its early days. "There was Durand Durant and the Human League and Blomage and the Thompson Twins and Soft Cell."

podcast.title: MTV Success and Early Video Investment
podcast.body: Duran Duran was identified as a "thin edge of the wedge" band from England, whose attractive and telegenic image led their label, EMI, to invest $200,000 in three video shoots in Sri Lanka. This investment proved successful, as their videos, particularly for "Rio," became early MTV favorites. The band's albums began selling out in cities like Oklahoma City, one of the few initial cable systems to carry MTV, demonstrating the channel's direct impact on record sales. "The industry finally knew that they were on to something when DeRan DeRan album started selling out in places like Oklahoma City just days after MTV started spinning the video."

podcast.title: New Romantic Origin
podcast.body: Duran Duran originated from the New Romantics scene, which began as a fashion movement in the UK in the late 1970s before adherents started creating music. Their unique style, blending punk, glam rock, and romantic period fashion, was central to the movement. "this was the origin of such groups as Durand Ran, Culture Club, Spandovalet, and a flock of Seagulls."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Romantic Origins
podcast.body: Emerged from the New Romanticism movement, drawing inspiration from nightclubs in London that played Technopop music. "Durand Durand came from this stew, so did the Culture Club."

podcast.title: Pioneering 80s Keyboard-Bass Alt Rock
podcast.body: Duran Duran was also mentioned as a "keyboard bass band" from the 1980s, whose music was central to the dance culture of alternative kids before grunge took over, and whose style saw a revival in the 2000s. "25 years earlier, long before Grunge guitars took over, alternative kids danced to keyboard bass bands like Depeche Mode, New Order, OMD, Durand Iran, the Human League, Eurasia, Eurythmics, and so many others."

xref.title: Band Decline (1986)
xref.body: By 1986, Missing Persons began to fall apart, coinciding with Warren Cuccurullo's opportunity to join Duran Duran. "But then in 1986, Missing Persons was falling apart."

xref.title: Departure from Duran Duran (2001)
xref.body: Warren Cuccurullo was asked to leave Duran Duran in 2001 because the band received an offer to reunite with their original lineup. Initially, the departure was amicable with a cash settlement, but it briefly became contentious before calming down. "Warren was asked to leave Durand Durand because the group had received an offer to reunite in their original form."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Entry into Adult Entertainment (2001)
xref.body: Around the time of his departure from Duran Duran in 2001, Warren Cuccurullo entered the adult entertainment industry. He first appeared naked in a game magazine in Brazil, which led to further similar photo shoots. His fan site was rebuilt in July 2001 to feature this adult content, predating platforms like OnlyFans. Even now, some of his videos are reportedly available on Pornhub. "Around the same time, Warren took his own plunge into the world of adult entertainment when he showed up naked in a game magazine in Brazil."

xref.title: Desired Interview Subjects
xref.body: The hosts expressed enthusiasm for interviewing iconic directors about classic videos, such as discussing Duran Duran's "Hungry Like a Wolf" video or hearing stories from directors who worked with Madonna and The Rolling Stones. "So imagine if you could go back in the days and sit down with Durand Durand and talk about the hungry like a wolf video, like what the hell could tell you guys being this jungle and just going through this crazy, crazy story and sitting down with like the best of the best and hearing their stories of the director is working with Madonna and working with the stones."

xref.title: Duran Duran Influence
xref.body: The band was overtly influenced by 80s groups such as Duran Duran, incorporating these inspirations into their sound. "The killers were part of this. They were unabashedly influenced by 80s groups like Doran-Doran."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Duran Duran Inspiration
xref.body: Before Eddie Vedder joined, Bad Radio's primary musical inspiration was Duran Duran, a sound that the band found wasn't working for them. "Before Eddie joined, the band's main inspiration was Durand Durand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Exemplar of 1980s Drum Sound
xref.body: The band, featuring Robert Palmer, members of Duran Duran, and drummer Tony Thompson, is highlighted as a prime example of the pervasive drum sound of the 1980s. This sound was characterized by its big, boomy, and powerful quality, often achieved by recording in large, reverberant rooms and augmenting with electronic effects like gated reverbs. "The Power Station featuring Robert Palmer, a couple of guys from Durandoran and drummer Tony Thompson. That is an example of the drum sound that was very much invoked in the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Music Questions People Almost Never Ask

xref.title: Highly Influential British Band
xref.body: Roxy Music is considered one of the most influential British bands of all time, with a profound impact on British punks, goth kids, New Romantics, and avant-garde artists. Their influence is evident in bands like Sex Pistols, Siouxsie and the Banshees, Duran Duran, The Smiths, Talking Heads, Radiohead, and Human League. "it's not an exaggeration to say that Roxy is one of the most influential British bands of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Joining Bad Radio
xref.body: Eddie Vedder secured his position as singer for Bad Radio largely due to a homemade demo where he covered Bruce Springsteen's "Atlantic City." The band had been inspired by Duran Duran but sought a new singer, leading to auditions where Eddie was chosen. "Eddie got the gig. And largely because they liked his homemade demo of him covering Bruce Springsteen's Atlantic City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: All members of The Killers are noted as big fans of The Smiths, Morrissey, The Cure, Blondie, and Duran Duran, drawing inspiration from these artists. "All the guys in the killers are also big fans of the Smiths and Morrissey and the cure and Blondie and Durand-Dorand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: The Bravery incorporated elements from Depeche Mode, The Cure, Echo & the Bunnymen, The Cars, and Duran Duran to create a sound that felt both new and familiar. Their music, released in 2005, prompted rhetorical questions about whether it was from 2005 or 1980. "They took bits of Depeche Mode, the cure, echo in the bunnyman, the cars, and Durand-Dorand to come up with something new yet very familiar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Notable Clients and Albums
xref.body: Over its decade of operation, AIR Montserrat hosted many major artists, including Bush, Elton John, Supertramp, The Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd, Duran Duran, Black Sabbath, Paul McCartney, and Dire Straits. Albums like *Brothers in Arms*, *Ghosts in the Machine*, and *Synchronicity* were recorded there. "Bush, Elton Johns, Super Tramp, The Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd, Durand Durand, Black Sabbath, Paul McCartney, Dire Straits, they all went to Air Studios Montserrat."

xref.title: Recruitment of Musicians for Band-Aid
xref.body: Bob Geldof initiated the Band-Aid project by reaching out to prominent musicians to create a charity single. His first call was to Midge Ure of Ultravox, followed by Sting of The Police, and Simon Le Bon of Duran Duran. As word spread, other notable artists such as Bono, David Bowie, and Paul Weller of The Jam, enthusiastically joined the effort, forming a supergroup of British talent. "First, he called mid-Jour of the band UltraVox. Sting of the police was called next, and Simon LeBawn of Durand Iran, and as words spread more people jumped on board."

xref.title: Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis
xref.body: Andy Taylor, the original bass player and a founding member of Duran Duran, publicly revealed in November 2022 that he has been diagnosed with Stage 4 prostate cancer. His severe health condition unfortunately prevented him from attending the band's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. "Andy Taylor, bass player and original member of Durand Durand, revealed in November 2022, that he has stage 4 prostate cancer and wasn't able to make it to the band's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame."
